answer: Coordination-priced action windows. Each identity’s actions unlock only after a randomized delay tied to prior unique interactions, so parallel accounts proceed no faster than one, forcing attackers to pay wall-clock time and continuous monitoring per sybil. A pigment of shared history tints each window, and any hollow cluster of fresh accounts stalls at the entrance rather than gaining throughput. The per-identity cost is the full idle duration plus a calibrated opal fee levied whenever a window is abandoned mid-delay.
